planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Variegata is one of the oldest and slowest-growing variegated Pieris selections, denser and smaller at maturity than the species.

directions: Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in dappled or partial shade, sheltered from strong afternoon sun and drying winter wind, and mulch to conserve soil moisture and acidity. Variegata is a long-established selection whose small, glossy leaves carry a crisp creamy-white margin, with new growth taking on a soft pink flush before settling into its two-tone summer color; its notably dense, slow-growing habit makes it a durable choice for a foundation planting or shaded border where a large shrub is not wanted. Lightly fragrant white, urn-shaped flowers hang in drooping clusters in early spring, drawing early bees. Water during dry spells while establishing and prune only lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds form soon after bloom, and remove any shoots that revert to plain green.

common_name: Debutante Pieris (True Dwarf Compact Evergreen Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Debutante is among the smallest Pieris cultivars available, staying under 3 ft at maturity.

directions: Site in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying winter wind, and mulch to help hold consistent soil moisture and acidity. Debutante is an RHS Award of Garden Merit selection prized as one of the truest dwarf Pieris, forming a tight, rounded mound of small dark-green leaves that stays notably compact and non-leggy compared with most japonica cultivars, making it well suited to small gardens, foundation plantings, and containers. Crowded, erect panicles of ivory-white, urn-shaped flowers open heavily from spring buds and are a valuable early nectar source for pollinators. Water during dry spells while establishing and prune only lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds set soon after bloom finishes.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society - Pieris japonica 'Debutante' (AGM plant)

common_name: Scarlett O'Hara Pieris (Red-Speckled White-Flowered Evergreen Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Scarlett O'Hara grows slowly into a larger, densely upright shrub than most compact Pieris cultivars.

directions: Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil rich in organic matter, in partial shade sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying winter wind, since foliage yellows quickly in alkaline soil. Scarlett O'Hara is valued for bright red new growth that matures to glossy dark green, paired with creamy-white, bell-shaped flowers flecked with fine red speckles that hang in drooping lily-of-the-valley-like clusters in early to mid spring. It grows slowly into a dense, upright, long-lived shrub that is larger at maturity than dwarf cultivars, so allow room in a shrub border or as a specimen. Water during dry spells while establishing and prune only lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds form soon after bloom finishes.

common_name: Flamingo Pieris (Hot Pink Bell-Flowered Evergreen Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Flamingo carries deep rose-red flower buds through winter before opening to hot pink bloom in early spring.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying winter wind, and mulch to help conserve soil moisture and acidity. Flamingo carries large, drooping chains of deep rose-red flower buds through the winter months, a striking display in its own right, before they open in late winter to early spring into hot pink, urn-shaped flowers that fade to a softer rose as they age. Coppery-bronze new growth in spring adds a second color echo to the display before maturing to dark glossy green. Water during dry spells while establishing and prune only lightly right after flowering, since next year's flower buds form soon after bloom finishes.

common_name: Bert Chandler Pieris (Salmon-Pink to Cream New-Growth Evergreen Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Bert Chandler is a rare Australian-raised sport prized for an unusually long, multi-stage new-growth color sequence.

directions: Site in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, protected from harsh afternoon sun and drying winter wind, and mulch to help hold consistent soil moisture and acidity. Bert Chandler is among the most colorful and least commonly offered Pieris selections, with new foliage emerging salmon-pink before passing through creamy white and pale green on its way to a mature dark green, so the shrub is in near-constant color flux through the growing season. Pendulous clusters of small white, lily-of-the-valley-like flowers open in early spring beneath the developing new growth. Its slower growth and smaller mature size than vigorous japonica cultivars suit a shaded border or specimen spot where the shifting foliage color can be observed up close. Water during dry spells while establishing and prune only lightly right after flowering.
